extracted.intended_audience: NOAA staff, other federal agency personnel, and Tribal officials engaged in government-to-government consultation and incorporation of Indigenous knowledge
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of NOAA and interagency documents, policies, and pointers that define standards and best practices for government-to-government consultation with federally recognized tribes and for engaging and incorporating Indigenous knowledge in federal decision‑making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular, meaningful, and robust consultation (E.O. 13175)
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 13175 charges federal departments and agencies to engage in regular, meaningful, and robust consultation with Tribal officials in the development of federal policies that have Tribal implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes a January 2021 Presidential Memorandum requiring departments and agencies to submit implementation plans for E.O. 13175; NOAA revised and updated its policies and guidance documents in response. This standard is the high‑level requirement for how federal policy-making must treat tribal consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: NOAA Procedures for Government-to-Government Consultation (Draft Handbook)
rubrics_metrics.description: NOAA Procedures for Government-to-Government Consultation With Federally Recognized Indian Tribes and Alaska Native Corporations (Draft Handbook).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as NOAA's operational procedures (draft handbook) implementing government‑to‑government consultation. The page lists this handbook as a primary implementation document alongside NOAA Administrative Order 218-8 and Indigenous Knowledge guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: NOAA Administrative Order 218-8 (Policy on Government-to-Government Consultation)
rubrics_metrics.description: NOAA Administrative Order 218-8, Policy on Government-to-Government Consultation with Federally Recognized Indian Tribes and Alaska Native Corporations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as NOAA's formal policy on government‑to‑government consultation; referenced as included/seeable in the draft handbook. Implies requirements and expectations for NOAA staff behavior and procedures when consulting with tribes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance and Best Practices for Engaging and Incorporating Indigenous Knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: NOAA Guidance and Best Practices for Engaging and Incorporating Indigenous Knowledge in Decision-Making (updated 5/20/2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that NOAA has explicit guidance on how to engage and incorporate Indigenous knowledge (IK) into decision‑making. The inclusion signals that federal action should include IK respectfully and according to best practices described in the guidance and appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal Resource Guide to the Department of Commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribal Resource Guide introduces Department policy regarding tribes, the Secretary's Senior Advisor for Native American Affairs, and contact information for each bureau's tribal liaisons to make it easier for tribes to interact with the Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide is framed as an implementation tool to improve collaboration with tribes and native businesses; it includes working links to resources, references to the U.S. trust responsibility and Self‑Determination Era advances, and contact information so tribes can more easily engage with bureaus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency coordination memorandum (NOAA–BOEM MOU)
rubrics_metrics.description: NOAA–BOEM Memorandum of Understanding to responsibly advance offshore wind energy (signed January 12, 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MOU is listed as an example of interagency coordination to advance projects (offshore wind) in a way described as 'responsible'—implying a standard that development actions should be advanced responsibly and with interagency and stakeholder coordination, including tribal considerations where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEQ role in NEPA: thorough, efficient reviews reflecting public and local input
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ) coordinates federal efforts and, as the agency responsible for implementing NEPA, works to ensure environmental reviews are thorough, efficient, and reflect the input of the public and local communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes an evaluative standard for environmental reviews under NEPA: reviews should be both substantive (thorough) and timely (efficient) and must incorporate public/local community input—criteria that are relevant to consultation with tribes on infrastructure and other federal actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain up-to-date Tribal Leaders contact information (BIA Directory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bureau of Indian Affairs’ Tribal Leaders Directory provides contact information for each federally recognized tribe and information about each BIA region and agency that provides services to a specific tribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the need for accessible, current contact information (interactive, map‑based directory) so agencies and others can identify and reach tribal leadership—an operational criterion supporting effective consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address GAO findings on hindrances to effective consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: The GAO report 'Tribal Consultation: Additional Federal Actions Needed for Infrastructure Projects (GAO‑19‑22)' examines key factors Indian tribes and select federal agencies identified that hinder effective consultation on impacts to natural and cultural resources and makes recommendations for improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This signals that agencies should consider GAO‑identified impediments and implement GAO recommendations to improve consultation quality for infrastructure projects (e.g., addressing procedural or informational barriers identified in the report).
